title: Add skeptic, logician and steward reviewers to your agent
summary: A developer building a package registry added skeptic, logician and long-term-cost reviewer agents to Claude Code; they report these caught a monitoring gap and a re-approval bug.
agent_role: Agents plan features, review the plan, build the change and submit it. Separate reviewer agents then check assumptions, logic and long-term costs. The human defines the features and keeps the overall process.
outcome: Author reports the reviewers caught a hidden gap in alerting, a logic bug that could re-approve rejected packages, and a change that would have created millions of search-indexed links.
what_they_did: The author builds Greenflagged with Claude Code. One agent plans each feature, several agents critique the plan, and another builds it and opens a change request. Special reviewers then check it. 'The Skeptic' tests claims, 'The Logician' checks reasoning, and 'The Steward' weighs long-term costs. Automatic tests run last.
how_it_went: The author says these reviewers stopped several real problems before release. One fix was a single page attribute that kept search engines from holding millions of login links.
worth_knowing: Agents still skip steps. One fixed a failing database setting but never restarted the service, so the fix didn't take effect. The author recommends having your agents write their own versions of these reviewer roles.
prompt: Set up three reviewer helpers for this project [repo]. A Skeptic checks every claim in a plan or change against the actual code and pushes back on anything unproven. A Logician checks whether each conclusion really follows from its premises. A Steward flags long-term costs like storage growth or search-engine side effects. For each change, run all three and give me their findings. Then propose fixes and wait for my approval before merging.

curation.rationale: A real Claude Code workflow with named reviewer agents and concrete bugs they caught. The builder-plus-reviewers idea has been covered before, but the specific roles and examples add value.
